security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU, cbo.clean/cbo.flush/cbo.inval (Zicbom) instructions invoke check_zicbom_access() at op_helper.c:211, which first probes for MMU_DATA_LOAD (read) permission, then falls back to probe_write() if read fails. Per the updated spec, cache-block management instructions are explicitly classified as requiring read permission and must raise a load access-fault/load page-fault (machine.adoc:3142-3145, supervisor.adoc:1388-1391). QEMU's write fallback violates this in two ways: (1) the raised exception is a store access-fault rather than the mandated load access-fault, and (2) on a hypothetically write-only region, the access would succeed when the spec requires a load access-fault.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: check_zicbom_access probe_write fallback path for CBO management instructions when probe_access_flags MMU_DATA_LOAD fails
security_spec.summary: CBO management instructions in QEMU fall back to write-permission probing when read-permission check fails, raising the wrong exception type (store vs load access-fault) and potentially permitting CBO access on non-readable regions contrary to explicit spec requirement

findings.finding: QEMU's check_zicbom_access() follows the CMO spec (cmo.adoc:352-361) which mandates store-type exceptions for cache-block management instructions. However, the updated ISA privilege manual at machine.adoc:3421-3423 and supervisor.adoc:1566-1568 explicitly reclassifies cache-block management instructions alongside loads, requiring load access-fault/load page-fault exceptions when read permission is absent. QEMU's write-fallback path probe_write() at line 249 raises store access-fault (RISCV_EXCP_STORE_AMO_ACCESS_FAULT) or store page-fault (RISCV_EXCP_STORE_PAGE_FAULT) instead of the mandated load access-fault (RISCV_EXCP_LOAD_ACCESS_FAULT) or load page-fault (RISCV_EXCP_LOAD_PAGE_FAULT). Additionally, on a write-only region, the fallback to probe_write succeeds when the spec now requires a load access-fault because read permission is absent.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction which accesses a physical address within a PMP region without read permissions raises a load access-fault exception.
Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

A cache-block management instruction is permitted to access the specified cache block whenever a load instruction or store instruction is permitted to access the corresponding physical addresses. If access to the cache block is not permitted, a cache-block management instruction raises a store page-fault or store guest-page-fault exception if address translation does not permit any access or raises a store access-fault exception otherwise.
